'''''Quercus'' × ''hispanica''''', commonly known as '''Spanish oak''', is tree in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Fagaceae]]. It is a semideciduous hybrid between the European trees Turkey oak (''[[Quercus cerris]]'') and cork oak (''[[Quercus suber]]'').

==Taxonomy==
The taxon was first described as the species ''Quercus hispanica'' by [[Jean-Baptiste Lamarck]] in 1785. {{As of|2024|October}}, [[Plants of the World Online]] treated it as the hybrid between the European species ''[[Quercus cerris]]'' (Turkey oak) and ''[[Quercus suber]]'' (cork oak) using the [[hybrid name]] ''Quercus'' × ''hispanica''.<ref name=POWO_296259-1>{{Cite POWO|title=''Quercus'' × ''hispanica'' Lam..|id=296259-1|access-date=2024-10-29|mode=cs1}}</ref> In this treatment, one of its many [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonyms]] is [[Quercus × crenata|''Quercus'' × ''crenata'']], which may also be treated as a separate species.<ref name=WFO>{{Cite WFO |title=''Quercus crenata'' Lam. |id=0000290347 |access-date=2020-10-29}}</ref>

==Distribution==
Hybridisation occurs naturally in southwestern Europe where both parent species occur.<ref>{{citation |author=Johnson, O. |author2=More, D.  |name-list-style=amp|title=Collins Tree Guide – The Most Complete Field Guide to the Trees of Britain and Europe|date=2004|page=220 |publisher=Collins|isbn= 978-0-00720771-8}}</ref> The '''Lucombe oak''' [[cultivar]] is frequently found in British collections. To be a true Lucombe oak, cultivars must be clones of the original hybrid arising in [[William Lucombe]]'s Exeter nursery.

==Cultivation==
A number of named [[cultivar]]s are grown in [[garden]]s, [[park]]s, [[Arboretum|arboreta]] and botanical gardens.

===Cultivars===
* ''Quercus'' × ''hispanica'' 'Lucombeana' ("Lucombe oak"), originally raised by [[William Lucombe]] at his Exeter, UK nursery in 1762. An early Lucombe Oak is  in [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|Kew Gardens]] arboretum, and is regarded as one of their 'heritage trees'.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.kew.org/kew-gardens/attractions/arboretum|title=About Kew's Arboretum|website=kew.org|access-date=28 August 2018}}</ref> The [[Tree Register of the British Isles]]−TROBI Champion is at Phear Park in [[Exmouth]], measuring {{convert|26|m|ft}} in height, with a [[diameter at breast height|trunk diameter]] of {{convert|261|cm|in}} in 2008.<ref>{{citation |author=Johnson, O.|title=Champion Trees of Britain & Ireland|date=2011|page=142|publisher=Kew Publishing, London|isbn=978-1842464526}}</ref>
* ''Quercus'' × ''hispanica'' 'Waasland' ("Waasland select oak"), leaves display an unusual slender, lobed shape.<ref>{{cite web |title=Quercus x hispanica 'Waasland' |url=https://www.ornamental-trees.co.uk/quercus-hispanica-waasland-p973 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200703142925/https://www.ornamental-trees.co.uk/quercus-hispanica-waasland-p973 |archive-date=2020-07-03 |access-date=28 August 2018 |website=ornamental-trees.co.uk}}</ref>
* ''Quercus'' × ''hispanica'' 'Wageningen' ("Wageningen oak")<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.majestictrees.co.uk/tree-shrub/950-quercus-x-hispanica-wageningen|title=Quercus x hispanica 'Wageningen'|website=majestictrees.co.uk|access-date=28 August 2018|archive-date=31 October 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181031005559/http://www.majestictrees.co.uk/tree-shrub/950-quercus-x-hispanica-wageningen|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* ''Quercus'' × ''hispanica'' 'Fulhamensis' ("Fulham oak")
